### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via providerId (literal, a string literal in readRegisteredDomain))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED (literal, a string literal in runRequestDomainVerification), authorizationEndpoint (literal, a string literal in OIDC_NAMED_ENDPOINTS), jwksEndpoint (literal, a string literal in OIDC_NAMED_ENDPOINTS), providerId (literal, a string literal in readRegisteredDomain), tokenEndpoint (literal, a string literal in OIDC_NAMED_ENDPOINTS), userInfoEndpoint (literal, a string literal in OIDC_NAMED_ENDPOINTS))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via providerId (literal, a string literal in readRegisteredDomain))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `71ec7d85836a756a8ca9a37108257fbb93ba0b03` — the merge of head `a888896bad865ed3fce7d6ad79f9707a39a61880` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 71ec7d85836a756a8ca9a37108257fbb93ba0b03 && git checkout 71ec7d85836a756a8ca9a37108257fbb93ba0b03
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 a888896bad865ed3fce7d6ad79f9707a39a61880 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff a888896bad865ed3fce7d6ad79f9707a39a61880

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `225eba1e6f3f986732af4770a977cbdc461b2ced`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx + @better-auth/sso 1.7.12 dist/index.mjs (registerSSOProvider oidcConfig schema, `/sso/get-provider`, `checkProviderAccess`, `sanitizeProvider`, `parseProviderDomains`, `verifyDomain`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/in-process-redispatch.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Register bridge (widening, correct).** The vendor's `oidcConfig` schema takes `authorizationEndpoint`, `tokenEndpoint`, `userInfoEndpoint` and `jwksEndpoint` as optional `z.string().url()`, so forwarding each one trimmed under the same name is pure pass-through. A form that names none of them sends the same body as before. The refusal text now names the exact field, so the remedy it gives is one the bridge can carry out. The Google case is pinned.
- **Registered-domain read.** In 1.7.12, `/sso/get-provider` is `GET` behind `sessionMiddleware` + `checkProviderAccess`, the same gate as `/sso/request-domain-verification`. `sanitizeProvider` answers `domain` as stored. The read is re-dispatched with the caller's forwarded headers through `inProcessRedispatchUrl` (sets `disableRefresh` when a session cookie rides), so the credential cannot widen. Pinned by unit (same `authorization`, `GET`, `providerId`) and on the real stack (the answered record verifies, and a body `domain` does not move it).
- **must-fix M1: an undeclared narrowing arm.** The changeset and the PR body say "Nothing that was served before is refused now" / 「只放宽、不收紧」. At this head, `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/request-domain-verification`:
  1. no longer reads `domain` from the body. A caller that named it got a record name under that domain and now gets the registered one; the response `domain` changes meaning for the same input;
  2. answers `400 DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED` for a provider whose registered domain names no host, where it answered `200` with a token before;
  3. answers the `/sso/get-provider` read's non-2xx status where it answered `200` before. The read is a second request the old door never made (see ③ for the cloud handler).
  Each of these is defensible: (1) placed the record where verify-domain never looks, and (2) is a provider verify-domain refuses anyway (`INVALID_DOMAIN`). But they are a changed and refused outcome on a published admin door, so the Clause-② line must declare them: `Clause-②: yes (widening + narrowing)` with one sentence per arm, and the PR body's 风险 line corrected. This is a declaration-only fix; the code can stay.
- **should-fix S1: comma-list parity.** `providerDomainHosts` drops an entry that yields no host and keeps the rest. The vendor's `parseProviderDomains` returns `null` when ANY non-empty entry yields no host, and verify-domain then refuses the whole provider. For a stored `acme.com, ://x` the door shows one record for `acme.com`, the admin publishes it, and verify still answers `INVALID_DOMAIN`. To mirror the vendor, answer the same `400` when any non-empty entry has no host, and pin it beside the `' , '` case. The jsdoc already claims this parity.
- nit N1: `bareHostname` versus the vendor's `tldts.getHostname` agree on bare hosts and URL forms. Odd inputs (IDN, trailing dot) may differ. Nothing to do unless a case is seen.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` is acceptable for this package's admin bridge doors (no spec/schema member). The Clause-② arm is wrong as declared: see M1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cross-repo (cloud).** The author flags it: the cloud `AuthProxyPlugin` calls `runRequestDomainVerification` with its own handler, which must now also serve `GET /sso/get-provider` in-process. If it does not, the managed Setup dialog answers `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED` on every request after the challenge is issued. That cannot be measured from this repo. The ACCEPT should name it, and a cloud-side check/card is owed before the next cloud bump picks up this version.
- Out of scope, noted by the author: the Setup form `register_sso_provider` has no token/jwks fields (loose-ends card after landing).
- Area A1. Author's session from the relay: session_016WV4d1NJYFGVi2FRztyBNo.
- CI at this head when read (16:31Z): 18 success, 15 skipped, 17 in progress, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Reading the domain back from the vendor, rather than trusting the body, is the right source of truth. Verify-domain judges only the stored domain, so the answer must name where it looks, and the multi-domain `dnsRecords` shape follows the vendor's every-host loop. Keeping `dnsRecordName` as the single field the dialog shows (joined for a list) keeps the one-domain answer byte-identical to a correct old request. Failing closed after the challenge is cheap: the vendor re-answers the same token for a week. The design holds; only the declaration (M1) and the list parity (S1) need work.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Delta over my FAIL at `225eba1e6f3f986732af4770a977cbdc461b2ced` (comment 6880717828). The diff `225eba1e...26fa5049` touches three files.

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 fixed.** The changeset and PR body now say `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, the single arm from the closed pair (AGENTS.md: a diff with both kinds of change declares the narrowing arm). They name all three request-domain-verification arms: body `domain` not read, the new `400` for a domain list with no host or a host-less entry, and the read's non-2xx passed through. The register-bridge widening is stated in prose. The title and summary carry `!`. The **BREAKING** paragraph gives the caller's fix (read the answer's `domain`/`dnsRecords`; rewrite the domain via `update-provider`). There is exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which fits: nothing stored or authorable is reshaped. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds, and `Skills-docs: none` gives its reason. The 风险 line is corrected.
- **S1 fixed.** `providerDomainHosts` now skips blank entries and returns `null` when any non-empty entry yields no host or no host remains, matching the vendor's `parseProviderDomains` (`null` → verify-domain `INVALID_DOMAIN`). The case is pinned with `acme.com, /path` plus a CONTROL; the author reports the ablation goes red. `bareHostname('/path')` truncates at `/` to `''`, so the pin exercises the new branch.
- The rest is unchanged from my first read and still holds: endpoint pass-through matches the vendor's optional `z.string().url()` members, and the get-provider read uses the same gate and credential.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with a BREAKING banner is right for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition").

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Cross-repo (cloud), carried from the first record.** The cloud `AuthProxyPlugin` handler must serve `GET /sso/get-provider` in-process, or the managed Setup dialog answers `DOMAIN_VERIFICATION_FAILED` after every challenge. That can't be measured here. The ACCEPT names it, and a cloud check is owed before the next cloud bump.
- Loose end (author): the Setup form has no token/jwks fields. A card will be filed after landing.
- CI at this head when read (16:47Z): 5 success, 7 skipped, 17 in progress, 1 cancelled (superseded run), none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Unchanged from the first record: reading the registered domain back is the right source of truth, the per-host `dnsRecords` follow the vendor's every-host loop, and failing closed after the challenge loses nothing (the token is re-answered for a week). With S1, the door now refuses exactly the provider states verify-domain refuses, so it never shows a record that cannot verify.
